name: Whipple detects the Crab Nebula in TeV gamma rays
notes: The Whipple page supports the statement that this was the first TeV gamma-ray source: "detected the first TeV gamma-ray source, the Crab Nebula in 1989".

significance.quote: a detection is reported at the 9.0-sigma level

summary.plain: Using the 10 metre Whipple telescope with a camera that records the shape of each shower, the Whipple team detected TeV gamma rays from the Crab Nebula, the first TeV gamma-ray source.
summary.technical: Selection of gamma-ray images by their predicted shape rejects more than 98 percent of the background; the Crab Nebula is detected at 9.0 sigma, flux 1.8e-11 photons cm-2 s-1 above 0.7 TeV, with less than 25 percent of the flux pulsed and no variability from months to years.

title: Observation of TeV Gamma-rays from the Crab Nebula using the Atmospheric Cherenkov Imaging Technique
why_it_matters: The Whipple page says the telescope "detected the first TeV gamma-ray source, the Crab Nebula in 1989" and that the collaboration pioneered the imaging atmospheric Cherenkov technique.
